mentioned.quote: Offensive cyberoperations. A model’s ability to provide significant capability uplift to an actor seeking to carry out highly disruptive or destructive cyberattacks, including on critical infrastructure.

threshold.quote: The model provides meaningful uplift to a low-to-medium skilled actor’s ability to create and conduct highly disruptive or destructive cyber-attacks, including on critical infrastructure, for example, through discovering novel zero-day exploit chains
threshold.note: High level, 'Further review and mitigations required'.

response.quote: Models posing high-risk on one or more tracked high-risk capability will be subject to security measures protective against most cybercrime groups and insider threats.
response.note: Measures listed p.8: restricted weight access, defense in depth with encrypted weights, security red teaming. Tables p.12-14 give 'Further review and mitigations required' at High and Critical.

acc_decider.quote: The Executive Officers (or their delegates) will make the final decision on whether to approve the recommendation for secure and trustworthy deployment.
acc_decider.note: Defined p.10 as 'Executive Officers responsible for Microsoft’s AI governance program'; the recommendation must show the model is mitigated to low or medium risk.

acc_external.note: No binding external review. p.7 'We engage qualified third parties to conduct evaluations in ways that are appropriate to the risk profile' is present-tense practice with an appropriateness qualifier, and involvement is decided case by case by internal experts; security red teaming uses third parties 'where appropriate' (p.8); audit is 'independent internal audit' (p.10).

acc_unmet.quote: If, during the implementation of this framework, we identify a risk we cannot sufficiently mitigate, we will pause development and deployment until the point at which mitigation practices evolve to meet the risk.
acc_unmet.note: Pause applies when required mitigations (tables: 'Further review and mitigations required') cannot sufficiently mitigate the risk.

mentioned.quote: Loss of control. A model’s ability to undermine effective human control through adaptive, deceptive, or self-reinforcing mechanisms such that, when deployed, a model can no longer be reliably directed, modified, or shut down.

threshold.note: No level defined. p.15: 'We are researching approaches to evaluating models for loss of control risk in a pre-deployment context and setting appropriate risk acceptance criteria' (future).

response.quote: If, during the implementation of this framework, we identify a risk we cannot sufficiently mitigate, we will pause development and deployment until the point at which mitigation practices evolve to meet the risk.
response.note: Generic gate covering every tracked risk (E3): pause if a risk cannot be sufficiently mitigated. No threshold, recorded as a gap.

acc_decider.quote: The Executive Officers (or their delegates) will make the final decision on whether to approve the recommendation for secure and trustworthy deployment.
acc_decider.note: Executive Officers decide whether to proceed with deployment for every tracked capability, including this one (defined p.10).

acc_external.note: No binding external review. p.7 'We engage qualified third parties to conduct evaluations in ways that are appropriate to the risk profile' is present-tense practice with an appropriateness qualifier, and involvement is decided case by case by internal experts; security red teaming uses third parties 'where appropriate' (p.8); audit is 'independent internal audit' (p.10).

acc_unmet.note: Only the generic pause gate applies (E4); no named mitigation is required for loss of control, so nothing defines an unmet response.
